Phelps holds 20 [Guinness World Records](/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records") which predominantly consist of accumulative Guinness World Records ("Guinness mosts", records formulated starting with "most") for total number of accomplishments and victories in swimming such as: most medals, consecutive number of medals, most medals within one tournament, most records in swimming etc.[[323]](#cite_note-323) It is the highest number of accumulative Guinness World Records held by an athlete.

1. Most world records set for swimming (male)
2. Most individual swimming Olympic gold medals
3. Most medals won at the FINA Swimming World Championships
4. Most Olympic gold medals in team swimming
5. Most medals won at the Olympics for swimming (male)
6. Most Men's World Swimmer of the Year Awards
7. Most Olympic golds at one Games (male)
8. Most gold medals won at the Olympics for an individual event (male)
9. Most FINA world records held by an individual
10. Most Olympic medals won, Men
11. Most consecutive Olympic swimming gold medals in the same event (male)
12. Fastest swim long course 400 metres medley (male)
13. Most gold medals won at the Olympics (male)
14. Most individual Olympic medals (male)
15. Most swimming Olympic medals won, men (single games)
16. Most Olympic medals won (single games), men
17. Most gold medals won at a single FINA World Championships (individual). He also won most gold medals in FINA world championship's history.
18. Most silver medals awarded in a single Olympic swimming race
19. Fastest swim short course relay 4 x 100 metres freestyle (male)
20. Fastest swim long course relay 4 x 200 metres freestyle (male)

Ascents of Mount Everest by year through 2010

The sun rising on Everest in 2011

By the end of 2010, there had been 5,104 summits by about 3,142 individuals, with 77 per cent accomplished since 2000.[[155]](#cite_note-8000ers-163) The summit was achieved in 7 of the 22 years from 1953 to 1974 and not missed between 1975 and 2014.[[155]](#cite_note-8000ers-163) An illustration of the explosion of popularity is provided by the number of daily ascents. Analysis of the [1996 Mount Everest disaster](/wiki/1996_Mount_Everest_disaster "1996 Mount Everest disaster") shows part of the blame was on the bottleneck caused by a large number of climbers (33 to 36) attempting to summit on the same day; this was unusually high at the time. By comparison, on 23 May 2010, the summit was reached by 169 climbers – more summits in a single day than in the 31 years from the first successful summit in 1953 to 1983.[[155]](#cite_note-8000ers-163) Nearly all attempts at the summit are done using one of two main routes. In 2005–07, more than half elected to use the more challenging, but cheaper northeast route. In 2008, the northeast route was closed by the Chinese government for the season, and the only people able to summit from the north that year were athletes [carrying the Olympic torch](/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics_summit_of_Mt._Everest "2008 Summer Olympics summit of Mt. Everest") for the [2008 Summer Olympics](/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics").[[156]](#cite_note-164) The route was closed to foreigners in 2009 in the run-up to the 50th anniversary of the Dalai Lama's exile.[[157]](#cite_note-165) These closures led to declining interest in the north route, and in 2010, two-thirds summitted from the south.[[155]](#cite_note-8000ers-163)

fanoutqa_030733.t: Miami Heat :: History :: 2003–2016: The Dwyane Wade era :: 2014–2016: Post-"Big Three" and rebuild :: chunk_0011
fanoutqa_030733.x:
Miami Heat :: History :: 2003–2016: The Dwyane Wade era :: 2014–2016: Post-"Big Three" and rebuild :: chunk_0011
On July 11, 2014, LeBron James announced on *[Sports Illustrated](/wiki/Sports_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")* 's website that after opting out of the final year of his contract, he would leave the Heat and return to the [Cleveland Cavaliers](/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers").[[27]](#cite_note-27) Wade and Bosh stayed in Miami. Like the Cavaliers in the 2010 off-season, the Heat focused on how it would maintain itself without LeBron. Wade and Bosh were joined by returning players [Mario Chalmers](/wiki/Mario_Chalmers "Mario Chalmers"), [Norris Cole](/wiki/Norris_Cole_(basketball) "Norris Cole (basketball)"), [Udonis Haslem](/wiki/Udonis_Haslem "Udonis Haslem") and [Chris Andersen](/wiki/Chris_Andersen "Chris Andersen") along with former rivals [Luol Deng](/wiki/Luol_Deng "Luol Deng") and [Danny Granger](/wiki/Danny_Granger "Danny Granger"). The Heat also drafted [Shabazz Napier](/wiki/Shabazz_Napier "Shabazz Napier") and [James Ennis](/wiki/James_Ennis_(basketball) "James Ennis (basketball)"). In 2015, they also gained [Goran Dragić](/wiki/Goran_Dragi%C4%87 "Goran Dragić") and his younger brother [Zoran Dragić](/wiki/Zoran_Dragi%C4%87 "Zoran Dragić").

After a season with several injuries, including to Chris Bosh and Josh McRoberts, the Heat finished with a 37–45 record, the NBA's 10th-worst. They failed to make the playoffs after being Eastern Conference champions four straight years. It was the second time in Wade's career they did not qualify for the postseason. The Heat were the first team since the [2004–05 Los Angeles Lakers](/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "2004–05 Los Angeles Lakers season") to miss the playoffs after going to the NBA Finals the previous year. Miami had qualified for the playoffs for six consecutive seasons.

At the 2015 [NBA draft lottery](/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery"), the Heat were awarded the 10th pick for the [2015 NBA draft](/wiki/2015_NBA_draft "2015 NBA draft"), which was used to select [Duke](/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils_men%27s_basketball "Duke Blue Devils men's basketball")

Kazakhstan :: Economy :: Economic competitiveness :: chunk_0036
According to the 2010–11 World Economic Forum in Global Competitiveness Report, Kazakhstan was ranked 72nd in the world in economic competitiveness.[[222]](#cite_note-229) One year later, the [Global Competitiveness Report](/wiki/Global_Competitiveness_Report "Global Competitiveness Report") ranked Kazakhstan 50th in most competitive markets.[[223]](#cite_note-230)

In the 2020 Doing Business Report by the World Bank, Kazakhstan ranked 25th globally and as the number one best country globally for protecting minority investors' rights.[[224]](#cite_note-231) Kazakhstan achieved its goal of entering the top 50 most competitive countries in 2013 and has maintained its position in the 2014–2015 World Economic Forum [Global Competitiveness Report](/wiki/Global_Competitiveness_Report "Global Competitiveness Report") that was published at the beginning of September 2014.[[225]](#cite_note-AT1-232) Kazakhstan is ahead of other states in the CIS in almost all of the report's pillars of competitiveness, including institutions, infrastructure, macroeconomic environment, higher education and training, goods market efficiency, labour market development, financial market development, technological readiness, market size, business sophistication and innovation, lagging behind only in the category of health and primary education.[[225]](#cite_note-AT1-232) The Global Competitiveness Index gives a score from 1 to 7 in each of these pillars, and Kazakhstan earned an overall score of 4.4.[[225]](#cite_note-AT1-232)

Swift has also provided one-off donations. She has donated items, including signed guitars and concert tickets, to various charities for auction, among them [MusiCares](/wiki/MusiCares "MusiCares"), [Global's Make Some Noise](/wiki/Global%27s_Make_Some_Noise "Global's Make Some Noise"), and [Rare Impact Fund](/wiki/Rare_Impact_Fund "Rare Impact Fund").[[547]](#cite_note-547)[[548]](#cite_note-548)[[549]](#cite_note-549) In 2007, Swift partnered with the Tennessee Association of Chiefs of Police to launch a campaign to protect children from online predators.[[550]](#cite_note-550) She has also encouraged youth to volunteer in their local communities as part of [Global Youth Service Day](/wiki/Global_Youth_Service_Day "Global Youth Service Day").[[551]](#cite_note-551) A promoter of children's literacy, Swift has donated money and books to schools across the US.[[552]](#cite_note-552)[[553]](#cite_note-553) In April 2018, Swift donated to the [Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network](/wiki/Rape,_Abuse_%26_Incest_National_Network "Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network") in honor of [Sexual Assault Awareness Month](/wiki/Sexual_Assault_Awareness_Month "Sexual Assault Awareness Month").[[554]](#cite_note-Dailey-2023-554) S

Shelley Wellons Moore Capito was born in [Glen Dale, West Virginia](/wiki/Glen_Dale,_West_Virginia "Glen Dale, West Virginia"), on November 26, 1953. She is the daughter of [Shelley](/wiki/Shelley_Riley_Moore "Shelley Riley Moore") (née Riley) and [Arch Alfred Moore Jr.](/wiki/Arch_A._Moore_Jr. "Arch A. Moore Jr."),[[1]](#cite_note-1) who served three terms as the state's [governor](/wiki/List_of_governors_of_West_Virginia "List of governors of West Virginia"). A resident of Charleston, Capito was educated at the [Holton-Arms School](/wiki/Holton-Arms_School "Holton-Arms School"), a private college-preparatory school in [Bethesda, Maryland](/wiki/Bethesda,_Maryland "Bethesda, Maryland");[[2]](#cite_note-2) [Duke University](/wiki/Duke_University "Duke University"), where she earned her bachelor's degree in [zoology](/wiki/Zoology "Zoology"); and the [University of Virginia School of Education and Human Development](/wiki/University_of_Virginia_School_of_Education_and_Human_Development "University of Virginia School of Education and Human Development"), where she earned her master's degree.[[3]](#cite_note-3) She is a member of [Kappa Kappa Gamma](/wiki/Kappa_Kappa_Gamma "Kappa Kappa Gamma") sorority[[4]](#cite_note-4) and represented West Virginia as the 1972 [Cherry Blossom Princess](/wiki/National_Cherry_Blossom_Festival "National Cherry Blossom Festival").[[5]](#cite_note-5)

After earning her master's degree, Capito was a career counselor at [West Virginia State University](/wiki/West_Virginia_State_University "West Virginia State University") and director of the educational information center for the West Virginia Board of Regents.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

Capito was elected to Kanawha County's seat in the [state House of Delegates](/wiki/West_Virginia_House_of_Delegates "West Virginia House of Delegates") in 1996, and served two terms, from 1996 to 2000.[[7]](#cite_note-:6-7)

For the [2009 race](/wiki/2009_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2009 Singapore Grand Prix"), the circuit was reprofiled slightly, including modifications to turns 1, 2 and 3 to aid overtaking, and also at turn 10 where high kerbs caused many accidents in [2008](/wiki/2008_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2008 Singapore Grand Prix").[[14]](#cite_note-15) [McLaren](/wiki/McLaren "McLaren") driver and reigning World Champion [Lewis Hamilton](/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") took pole position and sprinted away to win. [Timo Glock](/wiki/Timo_Glock "Timo Glock") finished second for [Toyota](/wiki/Toyota_Racing_(Formula_One_team) "Toyota Racing (Formula One team)"), and [Fernando Alonso](/wiki/Fernando_Alonso "Fernando Alonso") was third in the first race for Renault after they received a suspended disqualification from the sport for manipulating the previous year's race.

* [Pole position](/wiki/Pole_position "Pole position"): [Lewis Hamilton](/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") ([McLaren](/wiki/McLaren "McLaren")) – 1:47.891 (169.270 km/h)
* Race winner: [Lewis Hamilton](/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") ([McLaren](/wiki/McLaren "McLaren")) – 1:56:06.337 (61 laps)
* Fastest lap: [Fernando Alonso](/wiki/Fernando_Alonso "Fernando Alonso") ([Renault](/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One")) – 1:48.240 (168.725 km/h)
